hook_text: Your gate slides open from a motor that only spins. A gear and a flat gear make the switch.
clip_script: A rack is a gear flattened into a bar of teeth. A pinion is a small gear meshing with it. Turn the pinion, the rack slides. Round and round becomes back and forth, and it works the other way too. The sliding gate: rack on the gate, motor beside the driveway, limit switch stops it, a beam stops it for your dog, a release lets you push it in load shedding. Steering: the wheel turns a pinion, the pinion slides a rack across the car, rods turn the wheels. Maths: one turn moves the rack one tooth gap per pinion tooth. 12 teeth, 10 millimetres: 120 per turn. Bigger pinion, more travel, more effort.
visual_style: Whiteboard rack with a pinion rolling along it; a gate on a track with the motor box; a steering wheel, column, rack and tie rods; 12 x 10 = 120 written large.
mood: Everyday and practical, like explaining your own front gate.
pacing: Flat gear, slide, gate, steering, the sum, the trade.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count the teeth on a gate rack over one hand span.
